key_headlines.title: South Korea Raises 2026 Growth Forecast to 3% on Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: Government upgraded economic growth projection from 2.0% to 3.0%, reflecting strong semiconductor exports and investments. However, employment forecast was lowered to 150,000 new jobs, indicating jobless growth persists amid structural economic challenges.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Korea Expected to Raise Base Rate to 2.75% on July 16
key_headlines.summary: Market consensus points to base rate increase on July 16 with focus shifting to potential further hikes. Inflation and export strength raise expectations for rate reaching 3% by year-end amid government's 800 trillion won fiscal expansion.

key_headlines.title: Government Commits 1.35 Quadrillion Won to Semiconductor and AI Data Centers
key_headlines.summary: South Korea announced massive investment in semiconductor fabs (800 trillion won) and AI data centers (550 trillion won) to secure technological advantage. KIC will establish strategic investment accounts as part of comprehensive sovereign wealth fund expansion.

key_headlines.title: SK Chairman Chey Tae-won Calls for Reducing AI Costs Through Advanced Data Centers
key_headlines.summary: SK Group chairman identified high semiconductor costs and supply shortages as major AI industry bottlenecks. SK plans to invest approximately 1 quadrillion won to build 15GW-scale AI data centers in phased approach to address infrastructure structural improvements.

key_headlines.title: Real Estate Policy Debate Launches; Non-Apartment Supply Expansion Proposed
key_headlines.summary: First national real estate policy forum discussed housing supply expansion and regulatory reform. Building industry and Seoul city called for relaxing regulations on rental housing, non-apartment development, and resolving conflicts with local governments.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is entering an upward phase on the back of a semiconductor super-cycle, with the government raising its 2026 growth forecast to 3.0%, the highest in five years in real terms and the highest in 30 years in nominal terms. The upgraded projection reflects accelerating corporate investment and semiconductor export expansion, though employment gains have been downwardly revised to 150,000 new jobs, highlighting persistent jobless growth concerns. The government aims to achieve a potential growth rate of 3%, export ranking of 4th globally, and per capita GDP of $50,000, marking the start of an 'economic mega-leap.' Major risks include the 'three highs' (high inflation, high exchange rates, high interest rates), weak domestic consumption, and structural employment challenges.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government announced a comprehensive economic policy emphasizing semiconductor and AI investments as growth engines, with the upgrade of growth forecasts from 2.0% to 3.0% representing the strongest performance since the post-pandemic recovery. The projected nominal GDP growth rate increased from 2.9% to 9.0%, reflecting semiconductor export price effects, though this masks underlying employment weakness with job creation targets downwardly revised. The government is implementing an 800 trillion won fiscal expansion program while managing three major risks: persistent inflation, won depreciation pressure (trading near 1,500 won per dollar), and high interest rates. Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul announced the '3-4-5 vision' targeting 3% potential growth, 4th-place export ranking, and $50,000 per capita income, supported by mega-projects in semiconductors, AI, and future-oriented investments.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI ended 0.7% higher with foreign and institutional investors conducting net purchases of 4.1 trillion won, though the market experienced volatility with the index briefly breaking below 6,500. The KOSDAQ declined 1.9%, reflecting weakness in semiconductor and AI-related stocks amid global market uncertainty. The won-dollar exchange rate settled at 1,493 won, down from previous levels, supported by expectations of 40 trillion won dollar inflows from SK Hynix's Nasdaq listing offset by Middle East geopolitical tensions raising oil prices. Markets are pricing in approximately 50% probability of a 0.25% U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike by July 28-29, with inflation concerns and tariff-related pressures affecting both domestic and international sentiment.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's major manufacturing sectors including electric vehicles, batteries, steel, shipbuilding, and robotics are narrowing technology gaps with advanced nations while leading in some areas, driven by AI integration into manufacturing processes. Physical AI implementation is accelerating with telecommunications companies discovering new revenue opportunities, such as KT collaborating with HD Hyundai Samho for real-time data analysis and control systems in shipyards. Companies like Chaabi are participating in government-supported AI application projects including AI-based autonomous EV charging systems. South Korea and Gwangju are developing automotive semiconductor capabilities beyond memory chips, leveraging concentrated automotive supply chains and existing manufacturing infrastructure to become future competitive hubs.
sections.Real Estate: The government initiated a three-day national real estate policy forum to solicit public input on housing supply, financing, and taxation issues. Key discussion topics include expanding non-apartment housing supply, easing regulatory constraints on rental housing development, and resolving conflicts between central government and local authorities over development policies. Real estate experts highlighted the need for comprehensive, phased regulatory approaches rather than blanket restrictions affecting multiple regions simultaneously. The discussion also touched on property tax issues, with debate over optimal thresholds for high-value properties (ranging from 3-10 billion won) and whether increased holding taxes should be offset by reduced transfer taxes.
sections.International Economy: Global financial markets are experiencing a 'super week' with U.S. monetary policy expectations shifting as the Federal Reserve's July meeting approaches, with market probability of rate increase rising to approximately 50% as of mid-July. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical focus, with President Trump declaring renewal of maritime blockade against Iran and proposing 20% transit tolls, causing international crude prices to surge approximately 10% in a single day. The U.S. faces simultaneous pressures from Middle East geopolitical tensions, tariff-related inflation concerns, and evolving monetary policy expectations, with the June CPI report serving as a critical variable for September FOMC decisions. China continues expanding its African trade influence through port construction and supply chain integration, while discussions intensify regarding South Korea and Mexico's potential CPTPP membership, offering expanded FTA benefits and manufacturing competitiveness opportunities.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korea is positioning itself as a leader in AI infrastructure development through massive government investments and corporate participation, with SK Group committing to build 15GW-scale AI data centers to address the critical bottleneck of high computational costs. The government launched the 'AI for All' project to provide free AI services to all citizens, with Kakao, LG U+, Naver, SK Telecom, and KT all expressing participation interest, intensifying competition for building domestic AI capabilities. The gaming industry is identified as a key AI application frontier, though rapid tool-assisted game development is flooding Steam with 22% of 2025 releases disclosing AI use, yet capturing only 14% of player engagement compared to 2023, indicating quality and creativity remain critical differentiators. China is advancing industrial internet platforms integrating AI models with industry-specific intelligent agents, prompting South Korea to accelerate market-connected AI platform development to avoid falling further behind in enterprise AI solutions.
sections.Others: The government strengthened automotive emission standards, requiring freight and bus manufacturers to meet reduced greenhouse gas targets for 2027-2030, with non-compliance resulting in penalties, marking expanded environmental regulation beyond passenger vehicles. China is actively reshaping African trade networks through port investments and software platform deployment, having granted duty-free benefits to 53 African nations since May 2026 as part of broader resource security and supply chain dominance strategy. International crude oil prices experienced extreme volatility, surging nearly 10% in a single day following geopolitical tensions over the Strait of Hormuz, raising inflation concerns globally and impacting currency markets. Financial experts cautioned individual investors against leverage-heavy ETF strategies, particularly in semiconductor and AI stocks, recommending risk assessment frameworks similar to traffic light systems before large portfolio commitments.
